issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff who is treated as a party to the transaction and seeks to avoid a document must pay court fee for cancellation even when the relief is framed as a declaration that the document is null and void.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought declarations that several sale deeds were null and void and also sought a permanent injunction.
The plaintiff alleged that sale documents had been fabricated using signatures obtained on blank papers in connection with a proposed loan and agreement for sale.
The defendants sought rejection of the plaint unless court fee was paid under the provision governing cancellation of documents.
The Court treated the plaintiff as a party to the transaction and held that the substance of the relief sought was cancellation of the sale deeds.
issues.conclusion: The court fee was payable under Section 40 of the Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955, notwithstanding that the relief was framed as a declaration that the sale deeds were null and void. The orders refusing the defendants’ application were set aside, and the trial court was directed to allow time to pay the requisite court fee.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 40 of the Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955, a suit for cancellation of a document is valued by reference to the value of the subject matter of the document. A party to a document who seeks to avoid it must seek cancellation; framing the relief as a declaration does not change its substance. A non-executant seeking only a declaration that a document is invalid or not binding is differently situated and may be governed by Section 25(d). The Court relied on Chellakannu v. Kolanji and the distinction stated in Suhrid Singh alias Sardool Singh v. Randhir Singh, and considered Siddha Construction and G. Seethadevi; it also distinguished Shailendra Bhardwaj because that case concerned a state amendment not applicable here.

predicates.document_invalidation_suit: The plaintiff brings a suit seeking to invalidate a document affecting rights in property.
predicates.plaintiff_party_to_impugned_transaction: The plaintiff is treated as a party to the transaction from which the challenged document arose.
predicates.plaintiff_seeks_to_avoid_document: The plaintiff seeks relief that would set aside or avoid the challenged document, even if the requested relief is described as a declaration.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff treated as a party to the underlying transaction seeks to avoid a document in a document-invalidation suit, the applicable ruling is that cancellation court fee applies.

issues.legal_issue: Whether the court fee objection concerns the applicability of a statutory provision or merely the valuation of the suit determines whether the issue must be resolved by evidence.
material_facts: The defendants applied for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the plaintiff had paid inadequate court fee under the wrong provision.

The dispute concerned whether the pleaded claim attracted the provision for cancellation of documents or the provision for declaratory relief, rather than merely the numerical valuation of the property.
The High Court treated payment of court fee as a mixed question of fact and law to be decided on evidence.
issues.conclusion: The applicability of the relevant court-fee provision is distinct from the proper valuation of the suit and is not to be decided on the basis of evidence merely because valuation may involve factual questions. The defendants could raise the objection as to the applicable provision.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished the factual contest over proper valuation from the legal question of which court-fee provision governs the pleaded relief. It relied on A. Nawab John v. V.N. Subramaniyam and Rathnavarmaraja v. Vimla for the limited nature of a defendant’s role in contesting court fees, while holding that the distinction between valuation and applicability of a provision remains material. Section 12 of the Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955, permits a defendant to raise a contention about the proper court fee, but does not turn the legal question of the applicable provision into a matter requiring evidence.

predicates.court_fee_objection_in_suit: A defendant raises an objection in a suit that the plaintiff has not paid the proper court fee.
predicates.dispute_is_which_fee_provision_applies: The objection requires deciding which legal category of relief the pleaded claim falls within.
predicates.dispute_is_not_only_property_valuation: The dispute concerns the governing fee rule rather than only the amount or value assigned to the property.

issues.definition: When a court-fee objection in a suit concerns which fee provision governs the pleaded relief, rather than only property valuation, the ruling is that the provision is decided as a legal question without requiring evidence.
